title: How walks work

orient.question: What happens between Claude finishing research and you understanding it?
orient.answer: Claude sends a walk, a toast appears, you step through it and keep the recap.

example.name: Waivers TRD
example.line: Claude has just finished reading the delinquency waivers TRD for dvla.

steps.name: Step 1
steps.takeaway: A walk arrives as a corner toast, never a tab.
steps.body_html: When Claude finishes, it sends the walk to easel. easel files it under the project it came from and a small toast slides into the top-right corner.
steps.picture_html:
$ npm run test
you keep typing here
New walkdvla · Waivers TRD
steps.example_html: You are mid-command in the terminal. The Waivers TRD toast appears; your next keystroke still lands in the terminal.
steps.slower_html: Nothing opens and nothing steals your keyboard. The toast stays for 8 seconds. If three walks arrive at once they stack; a fourth becomes "+1 more".
steps.why_html: A tab you have to find is the reason easel felt unnatural. A toast tells you something is ready without breaking what you are doing.

check.prompt: Where does a new walk show up first?
check.expected: A small toast in the top-right corner

check.prompt: Does Ask need the Claude session that made the walk?
check.expected: No, it starts a fresh read-only call

recap: A walk arrives as a toast and never takes your keyboard.
Orient gives the answer and the size first.
Each step is one idea, with Slower and Why ready.
Ask answers from the walk's sources, even after the session closes.
Recaps and actions stay with the project.
